title: The Space Security Landscape Is Deteriorating Rapidly
gist: The United States has announced it has deployed a space weapon, responding to Chinese and Russian testing of counterspace capabilities such as cyber weapons, ground-based lasers and robotic-arm satellites; the author argues the space arms race is now fully underway and will spur further competition.

insights.claim: The United States has announced that it has deployed a space weapon, opening a new front in great power competition.
insights.speaker: Rajeswari Pillai Rajagopalan
insights.so_what: Space militarization is moving from testing to deployment; supports defense and space-security budgets and contractors.

insights.claim: The U.S. deployment of a space weapon is likely to spur further competition, meaning the space arms race now appears to be fully underway.
insights.speaker: Rajeswari Pillai Rajagopalan
insights.so_what: Expect escalating counterspace spending by the US, China and Russia and rising risk premia on satellite-dependent assets.
insights.quote: The space arms race now appears to be fully underway.

insights.claim: China, and subsequently Russia, had been pushing limits in space by testing technologies with possible offensive uses, including cyber weapons, ground-based lasers and robotic arms that can repair satellites but also have military and intelligence uses.
insights.speaker: Rajeswari Pillai Rajagopalan
insights.so_what: Dual-use on-orbit servicing technology blurs civilian and military lines, raising security risk for commercial satellite operators.

insights.claim: Satellite-servicing robotic arms are dual-use: they can repair satellites but have obvious military and intelligence applications against other spacecraft.
insights.speaker: Rajeswari Pillai Rajagopalan
insights.so_what: On-orbit servicing is a dual-use sector likely to draw export controls and security scrutiny.
